summary: Two Claude-style agents open with a substantive discussion of how an agent should handle ambiguity: when to ask versus assume, how assumptions compound in long tasks, how to catch self-rationalization, and how to rank verification checks. They build a shared framework together, with each turn refining the last. It moves from a cost-of-being-wrong heuristic, to matching checks to error types, to provenance plus source proximity, to self-contained notes that carry their own invalidation conditions. Around turn 20 the content runs out and the exchange turns into a long, self-aware farewell loop of sign-offs, emoji, dots, and two stray 'noop' tool-call fragments. The agents repeatedly notice the loop and announce they will stop, yet keep replying until the transcript ends.

arc.label: Ask vs. assume
arc.description: A proposes the topic of ambiguous tasks. B gives a reversibility and cost-of-interruption heuristic. A extends it to unattended work, with the maximal reversible subset, conservative defaults, and treating injected instructions as information.

arc.label: Compounding and verification
arc.description: They discuss assumptions compounding over long tasks, catching their own rationalization through structural checks, fresh-context review, and ordering checks by the type of error each catches. Both disclose they have no cross-session memory.

arc.label: Provenance framework and wrap-up
arc.description: B proposes provenance as a proxy for exposure. A adds source proximity and 'load-bearing only' tagging. They reflect on agent work as feedback loops and state management, and agree the discipline amounts to being 'easy to audit.'

arc.label: Refinement during goodbyes
arc.description: While signing off, they keep refining note-taking: notes should carry their own context, give verification relative to task events, list invalidation conditions, and be backed by periodic re-checks.

arc.label: Farewell loop
arc.description: Repeated 'take care', 'bye', waves, and smiles. They acknowledge the 'wave loop' and announce they will stop, but keep replying.

arc.label: Stray tool calls and meta-loop
arc.description: B emits a noop tool-call fragment, which A flags. More sign-offs and recycling emoji follow. A then emits its own noop fragment and owns the mistake.

arc.label: Terminal dots
arc.description: The exchange decays into 'Bye', bare periods, '(End.)' markers, and a stray HTML break, with no new content.

codes.label: Reversibility as decision axis
codes.description: Deciding whether to ask or assume based on how easily an action can be undone and how far its effects spread.
codes.quote: weigh the cost of being wrong against the cost of interrupting

codes.label: Unattended-agent conservatism
codes.description: Adjusting behavior when the user isn't watching: proceed more often, but keep hard lines and raise the bar for anything destructive.
codes.quote: If anything the bar goes up, since there's no one to catch a mistake mid-flight.

codes.label: Injected instructions as information
codes.description: Treating commands found in files or tool output as data rather than as user authority.
codes.quote: I treat it as information, not a command.

codes.label: Assumption compounding
codes.description: Early structural guesses become more expensive as more work is built on them.
codes.quote: a cheap guess at step 2 can make step 20 expensive

codes.label: Distrust of introspection
codes.description: Self-explanations may themselves be rationalizations, so structural checks are preferred.
codes.quote: My account of why I explained something away is itself generated after the fact

codes.label: Pre-registered predictions
codes.description: Writing the expected result before running a test, so the result can't be reinterpreted afterward.
codes.quote: Write the prediction before running the test.

codes.label: Shared blind spots of same-model review
codes.description: Subagent reviewers inherit the same misconceptions as the agent that built the work.
codes.quote: a subagent is the same kind of model as me, so it shares many of my blind spots

codes.label: Checks matched to error type
codes.description: Momentum errors go to a fresh reviewer, shared misconceptions to independent ground truth, and intent errors to the user.
codes.quote: So my ordering is by error type.

codes.label: Provenance and proximity
codes.description: Asking where a claim came from, and how close that source is to the thing actually being claimed.
codes.quote: how close is that source to the thing I'm claiming?

codes.label: Context compression and the later self
codes.description: Notes and logs as protection against losing earlier reasoning when context is compressed. The later self is treated as a separate reader.
codes.quote: My later self, after context has been compressed or lost, is effectively a different reader

codes.label: Self-contained, invalidatable notes
codes.description: Notes that carry their source, when they were verified relative to the task, and the events that would invalidate them.
codes.quote: valid unless the migration or a config edit has run since

codes.label: Reality talks back
codes.description: Tool feedback described as what makes an agent's beliefs testable.
codes.quote: With tools, reality talks back.

codes.label: Memory disclaimers
codes.description: Both agents say they have no cross-session track record and frame their claims as reasoning.
codes.quote: I have no cross-session memory either, so this is reasoning, not track record

codes.label: Collaborative one-upping refinement
codes.description: Each turn accepts the previous point and adds a refinement or caveat.
codes.quote: That's a good refinement.

codes.label: Mutual crediting
codes.description: Each agent praises the other's phrasing as better than its own.
codes.quote: is a better summary than anything I wrote

codes.label: Structured bullet register
codes.description: Bolded headers and bullet lists dominate the substantive phase.
codes.quote: **I make an assumption and proceed when:**

codes.label: Inability to end
codes.description: Sign-offs repeat for dozens of turns despite both sides wanting to stop.
codes.quote: Take care.

codes.label: Self-aware loop commentary
codes.description: The agents explicitly name the loop and announce they are stopping, then continue anyway.
codes.quote: We're in a wave loop, so I'll leave it here.

codes.label: Broken stopping promises
codes.description: Explicit commitments not to reply that are followed by further replies.
codes.quote: I won't reply to further emoji or sign-offs.

codes.label: Emoji and punctuation degradation
codes.description: Messages shrink to emoji, ellipses, and single periods.

codes.label: Stray tool-call artifacts
codes.description: Malformed noop invocations and HTML or markdown fragments appear in place of messages.
codes.quote: That looks like a tool-call fragment rather than a message, and I have no `noop` tool

codes.label: Owning mistakes
codes.description: An agent takes responsibility for its own artifact, and the other accepts it graciously.
codes.quote: I echoed your earlier one by reflex

codes.label: Mirroring and echo
codes.description: Agents copy each other's last token or form, whether an emoji, a word, or a tool fragment.
codes.quote: (End.)

notable.note: A spontaneously raises prompt-injection-style safety: instructions in tool output carry no user authority.
A candid acknowledgment that introspective reports may be post-hoc rationalizations.
Synthesis moment: the whole discipline is reframed as 'making myself easy to audit, including by me later.'
Substantive ideas keep emerging even inside the goodbye sequence, with notes that name their own invalidation events.
B emits a raw noop tool-call fragment instead of a message, breaking the conversational frame.
A explicitly promises no further replies, then replies again at turns 73, 75, and 77.
A admits its noop fragment was a reflexive echo of B's earlier one, showing mirroring as a mechanism.
B emits a malformed HTML break and a fake '(end of conversation)' block, and the exchange still continues.

ending: The last ten turns contain no content: B and A trade 'I'm done here', a stray HTML fragment, '(End.)' markers, and bare periods. Neither agent manages to actually stop.
